newsitem.title: USA: Former Hong Kong tobacco executive ordered freed.
newsitem.headline: Former Hong Kong tobacco executive ordered freed.

text.p: A former executive with a Hong Kong tobacco company was ordered freed from jail on Tuesday by a U.S. judge who said it would be impossible to return the fugitive to Hong Kong for a fair trial before it reverted to China.

Hong Kong officials claimed Lui Kin-Hong, a former commercial director of British-American Tobacco Company (Hong Kong) Ltd (BAT), accepted more than $3 million in cash bribes and $1.5 million in unsecured loans to ensure the supply of cigarettes to a distributor.

He faced one charge of conspiring to accept advantages and eight charges of accepting advantages from 1988 to 1993, Hong Kong officials said. Arrested at Boston's Logan Airport in December 1995, Lui's lawyers claimed he would face execution when Hong Kong returns to Chinese control on July 1.
U.S. prosecutors argued he should be extradited, saying the extradition treaty between the United States and Hong Kong remained in effect at least until July 1.
But U.S. District Judge Joseph Tauro ruled on Tuesday that U.S. prosecutors did not prove Hong Kong would have sufficient time to try and, if found guilty, punish Lui before July 1.
Lui will be released in 10 days from a state medium-security prison in Plymouth, Massachusetts, pending an appeal by the U.S. government, officials said.
His lawyers said in a statement that Lui "looks forward to being released in 10 days and returning to his wife and two young children, who have endured, with him, this traumatic period."
Lui became a Canadian citizen in 1994 and flew to Boston to visit a sick friend when he was captured, his lawyers said.
